text: The following question stood in the name of Dr Lim Wee Kiak – 5 To ask the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the immigration clearance disruption due to a computer glitch at ICA checkpoints on 31 March 2023 (a) whether there is a backup system to automatically take over the operations under such circumstances; (b) what is the standard procedure for any work carried out on major IT systems to anticipate any glitches; (c) why is upgrading work not done during off-peak hours; and (d) how many travellers have missed their flights and whether they are compensated.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry is satisfied with how ICA handled the recent service outage on 31 March 2023; and (b) how future outages can be prevented.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I invite the Member to seek clarifications today, if need be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the Member feels that his questions are addressed today, it may not be necessary for him to proceed with them during the next Sitting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The MMBS facilitates automated immigration clearance using travellers' biometrics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Unfortunately, the trial caused a severe system overload.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Automated clearance lanes at all the departure halls in Changi Airport, and certain automated lanes at Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints were impacted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The rest of the automated lanes, including those at the sea checkpoints, remained operational.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Prior to the incident, ICA had been upgrading its systems progressively and cautiously, with 10 out of 12 systems enhanced.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Only MMBS and one other system had not yet been upgraded.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For MMBS, the system upgrade would involve replicating the large biometric database to an upgraded system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This has to be done continuously over a few days and the MMBS has to remain operational during this period.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Our standard procedure for any system upgrade is to conduct tests in the User Acceptance Test (UAT) environment before deployment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Subsequent trials in the production environment were also stable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Next, we had planned to conduct further controlled trials during different times of the day, to ascertain that the system upgrade would not disrupt operations during the wee hours, off-peak hours and peak hours, before proceeding with the actual upgrade.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The wee hours trial was conducted on 15 March 2023, from 1.30 am to 3.30 am.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The trial on 31 March 2023, when the incident happened, was the off-peak hours trial, to take place from 10.00 am to 2.00 pm.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The vendors were on standby onsite and the plan was to recover the system within 30 minutes if the trial did not go well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The trial caused the storage systems to overload at about 10.40 am and the process was aborted immediately.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, the extent of the overload was much more severe than anticipated and the vendors who were onsite had to work with their global support team to diagnose and reboot the servers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the end, the recovery process took about four and a half hours, and MMBS recovered around 3.00 pm.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ICA immediately activated its Business Continuity Plan (BCP) once the system went down.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Off-duty officers were recalled to help man manual immigration counters and perform crowd control.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Across all the checkpoints, the failover process kicked in, and all the manual counters and certain automated lanes switched to back-up systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Not all the automated lanes have this failover capability, as different models were procured over the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At Woodlands Checkpoint, there was later another hour of delay for cars as the car arrival zone had to be converted to clear motorbikes manually.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: About 55,000 travellers passed through the two land checkpoints during the disruption.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Immigration clearance at the Airport's departure halls was significantly impacted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Travellers were re-directed to manual counters for immigration clearance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ICA immediately stepped up the manning of the manual counters through a combination of measures, such as recalling off-duty officers, deploying administrative staff and retaining the officers from the outgoing shift.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Changi Airport Group (CAG) assisted ICA by deploying additional Changi Youth Ambassadors and office staff, along with CAG's Duty Terminal Managers and their Customs, Immigration and Quarantine Team.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They helped identify travellers whose flights were departing soon, so that their departure clearance could be prioritised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Public announcements were also made to appeal for such travellers to step forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: During the disruption, about 30,000 passengers on 113 departure flights and 111 arrival flights, cleared immigration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These travellers were subsequently offered to rebook on alternative flights within a week at no extra cost.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In light of the incident, ICA is reviewing the approach to the upgrade.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The alternative approach that ICA was initially offered by the vendors was not tenable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It involved upgrading the system directly without replicating the database but may require five days of system downtime.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Even with the implementation of BCPs, degradation in service standards was inevitable, given the volume of travellers, and especially, at the onset of the incident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We apologise to affected travellers for the inconvenience caused and thank them for their understanding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I would also like to thank the ICA officers and CAG staff who had worked tirelessly, without complaint, to deal with the situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Going forward, ICA is in the process of implementing a multi-year plan, known as the New Clearance Concept (NCC), to transform immigration clearance across all the checkpoints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: NCC will provide more seamless clearance and help ICA, with limited manpower resources, cope with the ever-rising traveller volume.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Under NCC, all manual counters and automated lanes will be replaced in phases with the next generation Automated Border Clearance System (ABCS) gates, which will allow travellers to continue using automated clearance, even when MMBS is down.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: When they do, we will make sure we have robust contingency plans in place and try to recover as fast as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I hope for the public and Members' understanding.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Speaker, first, allow me to thank the ICA frontliners on what is, perhaps, is going to be the busiest weekend this year, with an estimated two million to pass through our checkpoints for this Hari Raya weekend.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One, during the period of the glitch, was there any loss or breach of data detected?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And in fact, ICA checks showed that there were no unusual activities found.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What we did was that we continued to verify the traveller's identity using the back-up system and also, just to be on the safe side, the ICA officers also did face-to-face checks with the passport for identification purposes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Speaker, Sir, we also like to thank the CAG staff for helping during the disruptions, to minimise the flight disruptions – only 21 passengers missed their flights, which is very commendable.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: One is that the Minister of State mentioned that during the disruptions at Changi Airport and the land checkpoints, the sea checkpoints were not affected.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And thirdly, how could we have some assurance that during this Hari Raya weekend, a similar thing will not happen again?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The travel volume at the sea checkpoint on 31 March 2023 was generally manageable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And, in fact, ICA manual counters across all checkpoints and the automated lanes at the sea checkpoints remained operational.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The passenger volume in that sea checkpoint were relatively low and travellers were able to clear via the automated lanes and they were not affected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I shared in my answer, some of the models of these lanes were procured at different periods.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, they responded differently to the whole process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, the trail was done at the backend common infrastructure that supports the MMBS system, which in turn supports all the checkpoints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it was not possible to conduct the trial, checkpoint by checkpoint, or just doing it at the sea checkpoint, or doing it in batches.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, in an effort to test the system load before proceeding with the actual upgrade, our approach was to conduct additional controlled trials during different times of the day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is something that we thought we should do so that we can prevent more serious disruptions when the system upgrade has been done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, as I have shared earlier, we have contingency and mitigation plans, whenever there are such disruptions that happen.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe some of your Clementi residents were affected by this?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I can indeed confirm there were Clementi residents who were affected and concerned by what happened.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I also want to put on record my thanks for the ICA and CAG officers who did their best under these unexpected and very difficult circumstances.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister two supplementary questions?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My second question is whether there are best practices throughout Government or internationally, on how we can take lessons from such situations to improve the resilience of our critical information infrastructure, especially at checkpoints where any delay can lead to very extensive backlogs and implications for Singapore's reputation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I shared earlier, we are actually at the frontier of technological development, with regard to clearance matters, especially border security.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If we look at what ICA has been doing, especially in recent years, it is really to see how we can improve technologically, to provide a more seamless experience and travel experience for the passengers, whichever checkpoints that they go through.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also have very good contacts with our counterparts overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: More often than not, they would like to come to learn from us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we are always open to learn from the other countries too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I assure the Member that this is a process that we have been undertaking and we want to make sure that we provide one of the best services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But looking into the security aspect of it, as Members know, it is not only about efficiency, but we must make sure that Singapore remains safe and secured.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the MMBS, currently, we have the back-up system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As we saw during the disruption, we were able to go into manual clearance and we were able to bring out other aspects of the BCP.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, when NCC is rolled out, this would be where, even though there will be disruptions, the system will enable the passenger to still be able to use the biometrics component in the travel experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we are essentially building a system that is more robust and will have more resiliency in the future.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have one supplementary question – whether there are any claims faced by ICA arising from the delays, coming from passengers or from any commercial companies?
